findings.title: coverage_progress criterion structurally ALWAYS TRUE — cumulative window design confirmed; metric does not measure actual coverage improvement
findings.delta: Confirmed via source code inspection. The coverage-tick resolver builds windows as cumulative 'since' queries: window[0] = last 1h, window[1] = last 2h, window[2] = last 3h, window[3] = last 4h. By construction, any traces in window[0] are included in window[1-3]. Therefore RL[0] <= RL[1] <= RL[2] <= RL[3] is mathematically guaranteed whenever any traces exist. The monotonicity check 'curr.RL > prev.RL' (where curr = older/longer lookback) is trivially satisfied. Current values confirm: RL=[7,9,10,11] newest-to-oldest (strictly increasing as guaranteed). coverage_progress=True.

evidence.command: docker exec substrate-live curl -sf -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8090/v2/impulses/resolve -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"impulse":{"type":"coverage_tick","pointer":{"type":"coverage_tick"}}}'

evidence.note: computeCountsForWindow queries traces with start_date >= since. Window i=1: last 1h. Window i=4: last 4h. Window 4 is a superset of window 1. Therefore RL[3] >= RL[2] >= RL[1] >= RL[0] always. The check `curr.RL > prev.RL` (curr=older=longer lookback) is satisfied whenever any new template is executed in any window. coverage_progress=True cannot distinguish 'coverage genuinely expanding' from 'we have any traces at all'.
Structural check confirmed: is RL[0]=7 < RL[1]=9 < RL[2]=10 < RL[3]=11? TRUE — as structurally guaranteed.
